stories.headline: Falcons WR Drake London cleared after being checked for concussion
stories.summary: Falcons wide receiver Drake London has been cleared after being removed from Sunday's game against the Chiefs late with a possible concussion.
stories.body:
Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London has been cleared after being removed from Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs late with a possible concussion, coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday.

London had six catches for 109 yards against the Chiefs in a 35-13 loss. He was removed in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a potential concussion and did not return in a game that was already essentially decided.

London has a team-high 801 receiving yards on 50 catches with one touchdown this season.

The Falcons have a bye this week before heading to face the Minnesota Vikings on the road on Thanksgiving weekend.

Stefanski also said that offensive coordinator Tommy Rees will remain the team's playcaller. Rees moved down to the sideline from the coaches' box for the first time Sunday, but the team's offense had similarly uneven results.

Stefanski said the coaching staff will take this bye week to self-scout on a deeper level and "with fresh eyes." He said the team has "to do better in multiple areas -- and then the first part of that is identifying those areas."

The Falcons have the sixth worst EPA per play on offense in the NFL (-0.16) and are 24th in points per game (20.1).

"I think we need to look at our process," Stefanski said. "A lot of this is we got to give the guys a plan that they can go execute, and we have to look at all the areas that we can do better there and then you have to execute said plan."

stories.headline: 76ers star LeBron James ruled out vs. Nets due to lower back management
stories.summary: LeBron James will miss Monday's game against the Nets as the 76ers continue to manage his lower back.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- LeBron James will miss Monday night's game against the Brooklyn Nets as the Philadelphia 76ers continue to manage his lower back.

The Sixers also announced that star center Joel Embiid, who was out for Sunday's win over the Indiana Pacers, is questionable Monday with right foot plantar fascia issues.

This will be the fourth game missed this season by James, who hasn't played both games in any of the Sixers' back-to-backs this season.

The Sixers are 3-0 without James, with wins over the Charlotte Hornets, Milwaukee Bucks and Toronto Raptors.

In Sunday night's win over the Pacers, James passed Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd for third all time on the NBA's career assist list. He finished the game with 15 points, seven rebounds and 11 assists.

James, who turns 42 next month, is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists per game this season.

Big men Dominick Barlow (back) and Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) were also ruled out for Monday's game.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey pickups: High-volume streamers to help replace injured stars
stories.summary: Begin your fantasy hockey week with forwards, defensemen, goalies and streamers to add to your lineup.
stories.body:
Mark your calendars: there are no NHL games on Friday. Toss in a two-game Monday and a three-game Wednesday, and daily lineup managers have some very thin nights to work with during the scoring period from Nov. 16 to Nov. 22.

The biggest news of the weekend came out of Colorado, where Nathan MacKinnon is expected out for a month and Cale Makar for about two weeks. The Colorado Avalanche play only twice this week, so the immediate fantasy damage is limited, but the ripple effects are worth watching. In the first game without MacKinnon, Brock Nelson slid into his spot between Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas. Nelson has dipped to 1.59 FPPG after posting 2.00 last season and is still available in more than a fifth of leagues, so he's worth grabbing if that promotion sticks. On the blue line, Devon Toews took over Makar's spot on the top power-play unit, a big boost for a defender already averaging 2.25 FPPG across his past 10 games. He's available in fewer than one in five leagues, so check your wire.

The week holds 47 games. The Buffalo Sabres, Chicago Blackhawks, Edmonton Oilers, Montreal Canadiens, St. Louis Blues and Vancouver Canucks get four apiece, while eight teams are stuck at two: the Avalanche, Detroit Red Wings, Florida Panthers, New Jersey Devils, Nashville Predators, New York Rangers, Seattle Kraken and San Jose Sharks. The Blackhawks have the best schedule of the week for both skaters and goalies.

The Utah Mammoth are the best streaming target in leagues with weekly transactions, with an average of only 11.67 other teams in action on their three game nights. The Canadiens (14.5) and Canucks (15.5) are next in line. Watch for 7:30 p.m. ET starts on Monday and Wednesday, plus afternoon puck drops at 1 p.m. on Saturday and 12:30 p.m. on Sunday.

Every Monday, we'll mine the waiver wire for lesser-rostered performers who have the potential to help fantasy teams in a variety of leagues. We'll also present several strong streaming candidates for the immediate week ahead.

More: Rankings | Most added/dropped | Mock Draft Lobby | Sign up

Most consistent players| Sustainable or lucky? | Biggest fantasy surprises

Forwards

Jackson Blake, RW, Carolina Hurricanes (1.92 FPPG, 30.8% available): Blake's line with Nikolaj Ehlers and Logan Stankoven is outscoring opponents 12-1 at 5-on-5 across 126 minutes, and it isn't a fluke: the trio controls 65.9 percent of the shot attempts, and its 13.0 attempts per 10 minutes rank 21st among the league's 275 regular lines. Add a spot on the top power-play unit and 10 points across the Hurricanes' past 10 games, and it's hard to see why he's still available in nearly a third of leagues. The Hurricanes don't play until Thursday, so this is a long-term add rather than a play for this week.

Evgeni Malkin, C/LW, Pittsburgh Penguins (1.80 FPPG, 33.9% available): A move onto a line with Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell has pushed Malkin's ice time to 21:16 a night over his past three games, more than three minutes above his season average. He's turned it into nine assists across his past eight games, and with Bryan Rust out until at least early December, there's no obvious reason for the Penguins to break up the trio. He posted 2.08 FPPG last season and is still available in a third of leagues.

Anton Lundell, C, Florida Panthers (1.63 FPPG, 76.7% available): Lundell has found his scoring touch since returning from a brief absence on Nov. 8, averaging 2.68 FPPG across five games, and a recent spot between Matthew and Brady Tkachuk explains a lot of it. With Aleksander Barkov out until at least late November, the Panthers need a center to drive that line. He's barely on the power play and Florida plays only twice this week, so this is a pickup for the weeks ahead.

Brayden Schenn, C/LW, New York Islanders (1.84 FPPG, 70.5% available): Schenn's line with Emil Heineman and Victor Eklund is 8-1 on goals at 5-on-5, and while the shot attempts are closer to even (48.4%), the results have him up to four points in his past three games. He's also on the Islanders' top power-play unit and logging 18:19 a night over his past three games, with Bo Horvat day-to-day and Calum Ritchie out until at least Dec. 1.

Shane Pinto, C/RW, Ottawa Senators (2.06 FPPG, 52.3% available): Seven goals across the Senators' past 10 games have pushed Pinto up to 44th among all skaters in fantasy points over the past two weeks. He's logging 21:30 a night over his past three games with William Eklund out until January, and the C/RW eligibility is a nice bonus. He's on the second power-play unit, so the goals are mostly coming at even strength, which makes them a little harder to bank on.

See also:

Rickard Rakell, LW/RW, Pittsburgh Penguins (1.71 FPPG, 39.1% available)

Joel Farabee, LW/RW, Calgary Flames (2.29 FPPG, 31.4% available)

Jack Roslovic, C/RW, Toronto Maple Leafs (1.94 FPPG, 41.7% available)

Pavel Zacha, C, Boston Bruins (1.65 FPPG, 51.1% available)

Defense

Mattias Samuelsson, D, Buffalo Sabres (1.88 FPPG, 33.1% available): Samuelsson keeps doing what he does: 38 blocked shots and 23 hits account for more than half of his fantasy points, and he's still skating more than 22 minutes a night next to Rasmus Dahlin. This week adds volume, with four games against opponents who combine for the fourth-friendliest slate for top-four defenders.

Pavel Mintyukov, D, Anaheim Ducks (1.68 FPPG, 94.6% available): Mintyukov has come back from a lower-body injury with a bigger role, logging 21:53 a night over his past three games and averaging 2.17 FPPG across eight games since his return. There's no power-play time, so blocked shots (30 so far) are doing much of the work, but he's available in nearly 95 percent of leagues.

Cole Hutson, D, Washington Capitals (1.91 FPPG, 45.8% available): Hutson has six points in his past three games and 11 across the Capitals' past 10, the kind of production that's hard to ignore from a defender available in nearly half of leagues. His pair is 9-4 on goals at 5-on-5, and its 12.0 shot attempts per 10 minutes rank 12th among the league's 210 regular pairs. His ice time is up to 21:16 a night over his past three games. Second-unit power-play time adds a little more upside.

See also:

Charle-Edouard D'Astous, D, Tampa Bay Lightning (1.99 FPPG, 51.6% available)

Philip Broberg, D, St. Louis Blues (1.85 FPPG, 46.2% available)

Justin Faulk, D, Detroit Red Wings (1.65 FPPG, 33.8% available)

Luke Hughes, D, New Jersey Devils (1.59 FPPG, 46.4% available)

Goaltenders

Tristan Jarry, G, Edmonton Oilers (3.24 FPP60, 65.2% available): Jarry has been on a tear, posting 7.15 FPP60 with four wins across his past five appearances. He's still sharing the Oilers crease with Devon Levi and Matt Tomkins, but with Frederik Andersen out until at least January, the starts are there for the taking, and Edmonton plays four times this week. The matchups are mostly middling, so this is about the hot hand more than the schedule.

Joonas Korpisalo, G, New York Rangers (5.40 FPP60, 93.3% available): Since returning from injury, Korpisalo has split the Rangers crease evenly with Dylan Garand, and he's made the most of his share, winning both starts with a .931 save percentage. That includes a 29-save effort against the Flames on Nov. 11 that was worth 7.8 fantasy points. With only two games and no top-10 matchups this week, he's a stash in deeper leagues rather than a streamer, but a true timeshare makes him worth watching. At the very least, it would be nice to see him win against teams other than the Flames and Kraken.

Jacob Markstrom, G, Florida Panthers (2.49 FPP60, 48.9% available): Back from injury, Markstrom has settled into an even split with Akira Schmid, taking five of the Panthers' past 10 starts and winning three of his past five appearances. It's only a two-game week, but Saturday's date with the Sabres is a top-10 matchup for fantasy goalies.

Daniil Tarasov, G, Detroit Red Wings (3.71 FPP60, 93.3% available): Tarasov has a .931 save percentage through nine appearances and has taken four of the Red Wings' past 10 starts in a split with John Gibson. The schedule is light, with only two games and no top-10 matchups, but he's worth stashing in deeper leagues in case the crease tips his way.

See also:

Dylan Garand, G, New York Rangers (2.45 FPP60, 50.7% available)

Devon Levi, G, Edmonton Oilers (3.63 FPP60, 49.9% available)

Adin Hill, G, Vegas Golden Knights (2.78 FPP60, 66.9% available)

Short-term streamers

Roman Kantserov, RW, Chicago Blackhawks (1.49 FPPG, 88.7% available): Kantserov has been on the ice for all of the Blackhawks' power-play time lately and skates with Connor Bedard at even strength, and he's turned that into six goals across Chicago's past 10 games. The 5-on-5 numbers are ugly (36.5% of the shot attempts), but the Blackhawks have four games against opponents who combine for the friendliest slate of the week for top-six forwards.

Kaiden Guhle, D, Montreal Canadiens (1.84 FPPG, 80.4% available): Guhle is a peripherals specialist, with 41 hits and 30 blocked shots making up nearly two-thirds of his fantasy points. That floor plays up in a week like this, with the Canadiens getting four games, two of them on light nights, against opponents who combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-four defenders.

Frank Nazar, C, Chicago Blackhawks (1.61 FPPG, 88.7% available): Like Kantserov, Nazar is a way into the Blackhawks' four-game week, and he's been the hotter of the two lately, ranking 39th among all skaters in fantasy points over the past two weeks. Five goals across Chicago's past 10 games and a near-permanent spot on the top power-play unit make him the safer bet of the pair.

Zach Benson, LW, Buffalo Sabres (1.59 FPPG, 67.8% available): Benson has gone cold, with no points in his past three games, but the underlying numbers say it won't last: his line with Tage Thompson and Peyton Krebs is 8-2 on goals at 5-on-5 with 59.8% of the shot attempts. He's also up to 4:44 a night on the top power-play unit over his past three games, and the Sabres play four times against opponents who combine for the fourth-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

Robert Thomas, C, St. Louis Blues (1.47 FPPG, 47.3% available): Thomas has been a disappointment at 1.47 FPPG after posting 2.01 last season, and nearly half of leagues have given up on him. This is the week to get back in: the Blues play four times against opponents who combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-six forwards, and he's still centering Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud with a spot on the top power-play unit.

Anthony Stolarz, G, Toronto Maple Leafs (2.02 FPP60, 74.6% available): Stolarz was a streamer here three weeks ago, and he's still splitting the Maple Leafs crease evenly with Sergei Bobrovsky, with five of the past 10 starts. This week the schedule does even more of the work: all three of Toronto's games are top-10 matchups for fantasy goalies, against the Blackhawks (third), Kings (sixth) and Blue Jackets (fifth). Whichever games he gets should be good ones.

For daily-league managers chasing goalie points, these netminders could draw the start against an opponent ranked in the top 10 for fantasy points allowed to goalies, and both have numbers worth trusting for a night. Crease decisions are anyone's guess, so treat these as possibilities, not projections, and confirm the starter before puck drop.

stories.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
stories.summary: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.

Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?

Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.

More: Best fits for top free agents | Latest on Skubal

Nov. 15

Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the New York Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.

Reliever Ryan Walker went to the Milwaukee Brewers in a trade that sent right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry to the San Francisco Giants.

Nov. 13

stories.headline: Nike replaces Adidas as UEFA ball provider to restyle Champions League
stories.summary: The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.
stories.body:
The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.

A match ball manufactured by Adidas, with the famous star-studded ball used for Europe's premier competition, will be used for the final time in the 2026-27 final.

There has been no confirmation as to whether the new Nike ball will retain the star pattern used in the competitions logo. UEFA said in a statement: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course.."

- Why the Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball could soon be replaced

From 2027-28, U.S. brand Nike will take over as the official ball supplier for UEFA for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League.

German brand Adidas had been the ball supplier for the UEFA Champions League since 2001 but their long-standing association with the competition is now coming to an end.

Nike went into exclusive talks in April with the agency that handles all commercial deals for UEFA club competitions, a subsidiary of United States-based Relevent.

Relevent was appointed last year by the commercial joint venture between UEFA and the increasingly influential European Football Clubs group, which has seen long-standing sponsor deals end.

Relevent was co-founded by Miami Dolphins owner Stephen Ross and also has a long-term deal with UEFA to market commercial rights for national team competitions.

Total broadcast and sponsor revenue for UEFA men's club competitions is projected to rise above 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) starting next season.

Camilo Andrade, Vice President and General Manager of Nike Football, said: "We are excited and honoured to return to the UEFA Champions League, one of football's biggest stages, after more than two decades, and to bring Nike match balls across UEFA's men's club competitions, including all three major competitions for the first time.

"Football is the world's game, and the ball is at the centre of it, the one thing every player, in every competition, has in common. This is a long-term commitment for Nike. We will listen to the athlete's voice, push the edges of innovation, honour the prestige and tradition of these competitions, and make sure the ball represents the instinct, creativity and joy football brings to billions of fans."

Guy-Laurent Epstein, Co-Managing Director UC3 -- which unites UEFA to Europe's clubs -- said: "We are delighted to welcome Nike as the official match ball provider for UEFA men's club competitions from 2027. Nike brings an incredible combination of sporting heritage, creativity and cultural influence, with an ability to connect with fans around the world. We look forward to working together, both on and off the pitch, to deliver innovation, quality and performance at every level of European club football."

Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: MLS Cup playoff Power Rankings: Can history-making Nashville be stopped?
stories.summary: Nashville just won the Supporters' Shield with a league-record points haul, so naturally it tops ESPN's MLS Cup playoff Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, and while MLS wasn't in action over the weekend in observance of the international break, the playoffs begin Thursday, which means it's the perfect time for ESPN's MLS Cup playoff Power Rankings.

Who's primed for a deep postseason run culminating in winning MLS Cup on Dec. 18? Which club with title aspirations is in jeopardy of an early exit? Joseph Lowery ranks all 18 playoff sides from first to worst.

1. Nashville SC
Final regular-season ranking: 1st

Conference seed: 1st in East

Next match: vs. Orlando City (8) or FC Cincinnati (9), Nov. 22, 8:30 p.m. ET

Not only did Nashville claim the Supporters' Shield as the best team in the regular season, but it also set MLS' single-season points record with 77 along the way. With a truly elite shot stopper in Brian Schwake, a back line with multiple Defender of the Year candidates, a flexible midfield and a star-studded attack, the Music City side has the tools to go all the way.

2. Vancouver Whitecaps
Final regular-season ranking: 6th

Conference seed: 1st in West

Next match: vs. Seattle Sounders (8) or Real Salt Lake (9), Nov. 22, 4 p.m. ET

There's a case to be made for the Whitecaps to top this list, given they led the league in expected goal (xG) differential this season. While Sebastian Berhalter's summer exit and Thomas Müller's recent fitness issues knock them out of contention for top spot in the rankings, don't be surprised if Vancouver makes it one step further than last year and lifts the championship trophy.

3. Inter Miami CF
Final regular-season ranking: 2nd

Conference seed: 2nd in East

Next match: vs. Columbus Crew (7), Nov. 21, 6 p.m. ET

It wasn't always pretty for Miami in 2026, with three different managers on the sideline over the course of the year, but moving on from Sergio Busquets and Jordi Alba was never going to be easy. Still, with Lionel Messi patrolling the attack and the most talented team in the league behind him, Inter Miami reminded viewers that they can hit heights no other MLS outfit can -- even if they have a lower floor than some of the other primary contenders.

4. Philadelphia Union
Final regular-season ranking: 7th

Conference seed: 6th in East

Next match: at New England Revolution (3), Nov. 21, 2 p.m. ET

If you'd merely glanced at this year's playoff bracket prior to reading this piece, perhaps you bristled at the sixth seed in the East landing this high. But after a league-worst run before the FIFA World Cup break, only Nashville posted more points than Philadelphia after the summer. Interim head coach Ryan Richter has his team humming heading into the postseason.

5. St. Louis City SC
Final regular-season ranking: 4th

Conference seed: 3rd in West

Next match: vs. LAFC (6), Nov. 23, 8 p.m. ET

Undoubtedly, St. Louis' rebuild is well ahead of schedule. After an offseason filled with front office and coaching changes, STL spent this season lifting the U.S. Open Cup trophy and setting a league record for consecutive games without a loss. Although a busy season seems to be taking its toll, City have both the talent and the tactical principles to make a deep run.

6. Chicago Fire
Final regular-season ranking: 5th

Conference seed: 4th in East

Next match: vs. Charlotte FC (5), Nov. 22, 6:30 p.m. ET

Robert Lewandowski's arrival in Chicago was supposed to supercharge the Fire. While that hasn't happened (their xG per game dropped from 2.15 before the former Bayern Munich and Barcelona star's arrival to 1.86 afterward), Gregg Berhalter's team is still among the deepest in this year's postseason field. No one should be surprised if the Fire's attack clicks this winter and propels them to a trophy.

7. New England Revolution
Final regular-season ranking: 3rd

Conference seed: 3rd in East

Next match: vs. Philadelphia Union (6), Nov. 21, 2 p.m. ET

Armed with Matt Turner in goal, who recently concluded the most dominant shot-stopping regular season in MLS history, according to American Soccer Analysis' goals prevented metric, the Revs won't be an easy team to beat. Really, though, they need a healthy combination of Jack Harrison and Peyton Miller to support Carles Gil in the attack if they are to enjoy a lengthy stay in the postseason.

8. San Jose Earthquakes
Final regular-season ranking: 12th

Conference seed: 4th in West

Next match: vs. Houston Dynamo (5), Nov. 24, 10 p.m. ET

Back at the beginning of the season, Niko Tsakiris and Timo Werner had the Earthquakes looking like world-beaters. Then, both of those dynamic attackers fell injured, and they have struggled to regain their full fitness ever since. They've started together just one time since August. That one time, however, came on Decision Day. If Tsakiris and Werner can stay on the field together in the playoffs, San Jose will have an outside chance.

9. FC Dallas
Final regular-season ranking: 8th

Conference seed: 2nd in West

Next match: vs. Portland Timbers (7), Nov. 21, 4 p.m. ET

Quite a lot changed for Dallas toward the end of the regular season: Daniel Job arrived in the summer transfer window to provide nearly unparalleled speed in the front line alongside Petar Musa, while manager Eric Quill appeared to rewrite some of his side's tactical programming. The result? A team that's more dangerous with the ball than ever before in 2026 but one that's even harder to predict.

10. Charlotte FC
Final regular-season ranking: 10th

Conference seed: 5th in East

Next match: at Chicago Fire (4), Nov. 22, 6:30 p.m. ET

One of MLS' models of consistency, Charlotte put together yet another solid season. While Dean Smith's team is far more dangerous in the attack this year than in the past with Pep Biel, Allan Saint-Maximin and some impressive young wingers leading the charge, it is also more vulnerable defensively. It's hard to picture this imbalanced Charlotte team sustaining a postseason run.

11. Columbus Crew
Final regular-season ranking: 18th

Conference seed: 7th in East

Next match: at Inter Miami (2), Nov. 21, 6 p.m. ET

After a brutal start to 2026 that featured a season-ending injury to striker Wessam Abou Ali and a coaching change, the Crew were incredibly busy during the summer window. Between their vigorous transfer business and the time spent under interim manager Laurent Courtois' tutelage, wins started coming for Columbus. Inconsistency still rules at times for the Crew, but they're certainly hot heading into the playoffs.

12. LAFC
Final regular-season ranking: 9th

Conference seed: 6th in West

Next match: at St. Louis City (3), Nov. 23, 8 p.m. ET

It's almost unthinkable that a team with Son Heung-Min, Denis Bouanga and tons of other quality players could be so bleak, but it's been that sort of year for LAFC. Those two superstars haven't linked up in the same way they did to close out last season. Marc Dos Santos failed to maximize them and paid for it with his job. Interim coach Xavi Tamarit hasn't cracked the code, either. Instead of a terrifying, forward-thinking outfit, LAFC have been scratching and clawing for results all season.

13. Portland Timbers
Final regular-season ranking: 19th

Conference seed: 7th in West

Next match: at FC Dallas (2), Nov. 21, 4 p.m. ET

It wasn't long ago that all signs pointed toward Portland missing out on the postseason. Instead, new manager Martí Cifuentes, who took over for Phil Neville midseason, has the Timbers playing an impressively cohesive style. Since the Spaniard's first game in charge, Portland ranks 10th in MLS in xG differential per game, according to American Soccer Analysis. Kristoffer Velde doesn't have enough help in the attack for this team to be a true threat, but progress is being made.

14. Houston Dynamo
Final regular-season ranking: 16th

Conference seed: 5th in West

Next match: at San Jose Earthquakes (4), Nov. 24, 10 p.m. ET

Although it finished fifth in the West, no playoff team scored fewer goals in the regular season than Houston. It's those attacking limitations that will hold the Dynamo back in the playoffs. Outside of Brazilian newcomer Guilherme, they lack the sort of repeatable chance creation that fuels a run to MLS Cup.

15. Seattle Sounders
Final regular-season ranking: 13th

Conference seed: 8th in West

Next match: vs. Real Salt Lake (9), Nov. 19, 10 p.m. ET

Fully healthy and able to lean on their mixture of talent and experience, the Sounders would be a threat to win MLS Cup, but manager Brian Schmetzer simply doesn't have a complete squad at his disposal -- nor has he for most of the year. Jordan Morris' first-half exit on Decision Day was just the latest in a long line of fitness issues that have turned Seattle's season upside down.

16. Real Salt Lake
Final regular-season ranking: 21st

Conference seed: 8th in East

Next match: at Seattle Sounders (8), Nov. 19, 10 p.m. ET

With Zavier Gozo and Diego Luna still in the lineup, lifting a trophy would have been possible for Salt Lake. With Gozo now playing for Crystal Palace after a summer move and Luna out for the year with an injury, RSL are simply too short on weapons. There are quality players in Utah, but a postseason path that begins with a road game in Seattle before a potential Vancouver series will be too much to handle.

17. Orlando City
Final regular-season ranking: 11th

Conference seed: 8th in East

Next match: vs. FC Cincinnati (9), Nov. 19, 7:30 p.m. ET

As brilliant as Antoine Griezmann is, even the best player in MLS not named Lionel Messi can't paper over all the cracks in Orlando's defensive setup. Orlando City conceded 78 goals in the regular season, good for the second most in one campaign in league history. There's an entire season's worth of evidence that points to Orlando's inability to control leads, win games and lift a trophy.

So many of Orlando City's issues also apply to Cincinnati: Pat Noonan's team conceded a staggering 75 goals and had to be rescued by brilliant attacking play in the regular season. Like Orlando, Cincinnati lacks the defensive consistency to win a wild-card game and handle business on the road this winter.

stories.headline: Kayla Harrison could take on a familiar foe in next fight
stories.summary: What options do Ciryl Gane and Kayla Harrison have after the first defenses of their titles at UFC 334?
stories.body:
Two UFC champions successfully defended their titles for the first time atop the UFC 334 fight card at Madison Square Garden in New York on Saturday. But the victories left the two titleholders in drastically different positions.

Heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defeated Josh Hokit by unanimous decision in the main event, putting himself in position to face a selected list of challengers, many of whom were ranked ahead of Hokit in ESPN's divisional rankings entering last weekend's fight card.

In the co-main event, women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison spoiled Amanda Nunes' highly anticipated return from retirement, submitting the two-time titleholder in Round 4. Despite making just one title defense, Harrison appears to have limited options ahead.

Here are the most likely scenarios for each of the top stars from UFC 334 moving forward.

Ciryl Gane, heavyweight champion

Who should be next: Alexander Volkov

It's not the most blockbuster matchup, but it's the right fight to make. I wrote this in October, when Volkov defeated Rizvan Kuniev for his third straight win. Volkov is 7-1 in his past eight fights, with the only loss coming to Gane via split decision in a 2024 bout that many observers thought Volkov should have won. For the past two years, Volkov has been a gatekeeper for the division. There are legitimate cases for different matchups, but Volkov is the most deserving heavyweight title challenger. This division has been stop-and-go for several years, at times because the UFC was looking to make the big fight. It's time to book the fight that makes the most sense and pair Gane with Volkov.

Wild card: Tom Aspinall

If Aspinall gets cleared to fight again and returns from an eye injury, this fight immediately jumps to the top of the list. But the former champion has been quiet lately. This matchup probably won't be talked about much until Aspinall himself breaks his silence.

Josh Hokit, heavyweight

Who should be next: Alex Pereira

Pereira will face Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 in December. Win or lose, Hokit should be next, and that should be expected. I don't expect Pereira to look past Pavlovich, but I think it makes sense for all parties involved to commit to that fight now. Hokit's stock has never been higher and Pereira is in uncharted territory for the first time in his MMA career. Is he going to stay at heavyweight? Is he losing a step at age 39? Hokit has done a wonderful job of building this fight already. The sooner this fight happens, the better. It's not a fight the UFC needs to let marinate.

Wild card: Pavlovich

Depending on how the fight in December goes and what the UFC decides to do with Gane's next title defense, Hokit's next opponent could certainly be Pavlovich. Still, I have a hard time envisioning a scenario that would make more sense than Pereira.

Kayla Harrison, women's bantamweight champion
Who should be next: Rematch at featherweight

Harrison shared this option during fight week, saying she would offer a 145-pound rematch to Nunes if she beat her Saturday. It's the only fight for both. Let's not kid ourselves. There is nothing at 135 pounds worth Harrison's or Nunes' attention, outside of fighting each other again. The only potential exception is Valentina Shevchenko, but Harrison is so much bigger than Shevchenko. It's not a bad matchup, and under different circumstances, I might even advocate for it. But the truth is, Harrison doesn't have many fights left, and she doesn't want to make 135 pounds again. I don't think she needs to. With a different game plan and less ring rust, Nunes is still an interesting matchup for Harrison. Do it at featherweight, and they can retire after.

Uroš Medić, welterweight

Who should be next: Belal Muhammad

On one hand, Medić didn't look particularly great against an opponent who is much lower in the UFC's rankings, in a fight that was scored a majority draw. On the other hand, he would have won were it not for a point deduction for two low kicks that might have compromised Kevin Holland. In which case, I think we just throw the whole thing out, right? So, where does that leave us? It's not clear what to do with Medić, just as it's not clear what to do with Muhammad, coming off three consecutive losses. This fight might not generate much excitement, but it would at least bring some clarity to the division.

Wild card: Leon Edwards

Edwards is in the same situation as Muhammad. He's a former champion who is riding a three-fight skid. Several former champions currently occupy spots in the UFC's welterweight rankings, including Muhammad, Edwards, Kamaru Usman and Jack Della Maddalena. You can expect the UFC to match some of these veterans with young contenders to bring clarity to the division.

Kevin Holland, welterweight/middleweight
Who should be next: Christian Leroy Duncan

Welterweight is a better division for Holland than middleweight. That's not really up for debate. But he's a chameleon when it comes to switching divisions. He goes where he's needed, where the better fight is. In this case, I think his next fight should be at middleweight. Some will say I'm off base, pairing him with a top-10 ranked middleweight, and that's fair. But Leroy Duncan is coming off a disappointing loss to Brendan Allen in his first main event in October. Leroy Duncan still has potential as someone the UFC can build around, with an exciting style. There are a few possible matchups for him in the top 15, but nothing that really stands out. A fan-friendly fight against Holland would likely do more for his profile than just about any ranked matchup. I would like to see the UFC think outside the box with this one.

Wild card: Geoff Neal

Neal has faced hard times, losing four of his past five fights, including the last two by knockout. Expectations have obviously fallen, but Neal is still known for an exciting style. Neal and Holland first fought in 2017, before both signed with the UFC. The promotion has tried to book a rematch, but it hasn't happened thus far. It would be an appropriate time to revisit this matchup.

Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.

Lando Norris clinched his third victory this season at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead in wet conditions.

Max Verstappen had a masterful drive in his Red Bull and charged his way through the field from 21st to second.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 21st round.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Las Vegas Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit
Las Vegas' race is certainly one of the most newest and flashiest street races with one of the most famous backdrops in the world after it took a spot on the F1 calendar in 2023, costing around $500 million.

The street circuit is one of few night races on the calendar, and includes the city's famous Strip and different landmarks around the city, such as the Bellagio and the Sphere.

The best place to watch the action unfold is from a casino, or West Harmon Zone grandstands. Casinos offer high-end packages to watch in specially built race zones around the circuit, but the grandstands around the final corner and viewing the pit straight still offer a great view.

Most poles: Charles Leclerc (2023), Russell (2024) and Norris (2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Las Vegas Grand Prix is cold with temperatures between 10-14°C.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Norris continued his impressive form in the business end of the season and put in a blistering lap to take pole position.

But come Sunday's race he ran wide at the first corner in an attempt to hold off Red Bull's Verstappen, who took advantage from second to gain the lead.

The Dutchman controlled the lead from that point onwards to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Norris and Oscar Piastri ended up being disqualified from the race for a technical infringement -- a major blow in the title race with only two races to go at the time.

Who will win this year?

Mercedes completed the double and wrapped up the constructors' championship last time out, a week after Antonelli was crowned world champion.

With it being a night race, the conditions in Las Vegas are always very cold, a world away from some of the soaring temperatures the drivers race in throughout the year.

McLaren has been running a heavily-upgraded car that seems to be working well, and Norris will be carrying his winning momentum to Vegas.

Verstappen is in strong form and has made his way to second in the title standings with three victories under his belt and 12 podiums this year.

Having won twice in Vegas already, the Dutchman will certainly be the one to watch.

stories.headline: Toronto Tempo win 2027 WNBA draft lottery, land No. 1 pick
stories.summary: The Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery Sunday night, earning the No. 1 pick and potentially the chance to draft USC star JuJu Watkins. The Comets will choose second, followed by the Mystics.
stories.body:
The Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft after winning the draft lottery Sunday night.

After completing its inaugural season in 2026, Toronto becomes the first franchise to have the top pick heading into its second season since the Dream in 2009, when Atlanta selected Angel McCoughtry. The Tempo will make their selection April 12.

Lottery odds are based on teams' two-year cumulative records, except for Portland and Toronto, which were expansion teams in 2026. Their odds were solely based on their records from this past season.

The Houston Comets, formerly the Connecticut Sun (22-66), and Toronto (11-33) had the best odds to land the No. 1 pick, each with 329 chances out of 1,000. This marked the first time since 2015 that two teams had the same odds for the first selection.

The Sun, relocating to Texas from Connecticut this offseason, went 1-2 against Toronto in 2026 -- which is the first tiebreaker -- so the franchise couldn't fall past the third pick. Toronto was guaranteed at least the fourth selection.

"I [felt] like something amazing was going to happen," said Tempo forward Aneesah Morrow, the team's lottery representative. "We're here now ... The future is bright. We have great and amazing players, and we have a country on our back. It feels different when you play like that."

Houston will select second in the draft. All of the other selections are in line with what the odds projected heading into Sunday. Washington, which had the next-best odds after acquiring Chicago's first-round pick in the trade that sent Ariel Atkins to the Sky, will pick third.

Seattle will select at No. 4, followed by Portland at No. 5. The Los Angeles Sparks have the sixth and seventh picks -- one that is their own and the other acquired from Phoenix in the Kelsey Plum trade in August.

USC's JuJu Watkins is projected to go No. 1 in ESPN's latest mock draft released Thursday, with Texas' Madison Booker slotted at No. 2.

Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo, Virginia's Kymora Johnson, LSU's Mikaylah Williams, Kansas' S'Mya Nichols and Sarah Cisse of France are projected to round out the lottery picks.

The Tempo had a strong start to their season before veteran Brittney Sykes was sidelined indefinitely because of a plantar fascia injury. After she went down, Toronto went 4-21, including a 12-game losing streak. But Sykes and Marina Mabrey combined to form one of the highest-scoring backcourts in the league.

Toronto has some young talent in Morrow, whom the team acquired in a midseason trade, and last year's No. 6 pick Kiki Rice, who was the team's third-leading scorer but missed nearly two months because of a Grade 2 left ankle sprain. The combination of Mabrey, Sykes and Rice gives the Tempo perimeter depth. However, they are somewhat thin in the front court.

"[Toronto] is amazing," Morrow said. "Ever since I walked in the locker room, from the beginning, I was able to see the chemistry ... it's all about building the future of the Toronto franchise."

The WNBA schedule will increase from 44 to 50 games in the 2027 season, making it the longest in league history. The added games were part of the new collective bargaining agreement, which also vastly increased pay, secured a $2.2 billion media deal and slated six expansion teams to join the league between 2024 and 2030.

The 2027 WNBA season is expected to start May 7 and has a latest possible end date of Oct. 24, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou last week.

"We're excited about the momentum; it's never been stronger," said Bethany Donaphin, senior vice president and head of WNBA league operations. "We think there's a demand, and we're excited to expand to 50 games."

The rest of the first-round draft order is: No. 8 New York, No. 9 Dallas, No. 10 Indiana, No. 11 Chicago, No. 12 Chicago, No. 13 Dallas, No. 14 Golden State and No. 15 Minnesota.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: When will the Chargers finally win? Here are the odds and our best bets
stories.summary: The Chargers are 0-8 heading into their Monday night matchup with the Ravens. If they don't win this week, when will they get off the schneid?
stories.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers came into the 2026-27 season with Super Bowl aspirations. On opening night of the season, the Chargers were 17-1 to win the championship. Only the Los Angeles Rams (+500), Baltimore Ravens (10-1), Buffalo Bills (10-1), Seattle Seahawks (12-1) and Kansas City Chiefs (16-1) had shorter odds.

My, how things have changed. The Chargers enter Week 10 winless at 0-8 and are 1000-1 to win the Super Bowl. Offerings for them to make the playoffs are no longer even on the board. They have been outscored by 98 points, easily the worst differential in the league.

So when will win No. 1 come? According to the odds at DraftKings, the Chargers' best chance comes in Week 11 against the New York Jets (+125). Their second-best opportunity? That comes Monday night, where they are +185 to notch their first win against the Ravens. The Chargers are 4.5-point road underdogs, but FPI is more optimistic, giving them a 56.1% chance to win.

Things get a little dicier if they don't get out of the win column in the next two weeks.

If not now, when? We asked our betting analysts to give their predictions for when the Chargers would finally get off the schneid.

Week 11 vs. Jets (+125)

Pamela Maldonado: Miami is in the conversation, but that game is weeks away. The Jets are the best immediate opportunity. New York's defense doesn't create many of the problems that have wrecked the Chargers. The Jets struggle against the run and have intercepted just two passes. That should give Justin Herbert a cleaner game, one that can allow Omarion Hampton to carry more of the offense. It's difficult to trust the Chargers, but a matchup against the Jets asks far less of Herbert.

Eric Moody: The Chargers are 4.5-point road underdogs against the Ravens on Monday night but are already early 3-point home favorites against the Jets in Week 11. New York has lost five consecutive games and could be without Geno Smith, who suffered an ankle injury against the Bills on Sunday. Rookie Cade Klubnik could make his first NFL start. I expect the Chargers to lose in Baltimore, but I like Herbert's chances of getting Los Angeles its first win at home against a struggling 2-8 Jets team.

Week 12 vs. Patriots (+500)

Matt Bowen: This New England Patriots offense will regress with Tommy DeVito under center. He's a lower-level No. 2 quarterback. And A.J. Brown (hamstring) could be down again for the Week 12 matchup. Can the Chargers steal one here? Yes, if Herbert can play with better decision making. Let's take the odds here.

The NBA starts this week with a solid eight-game slate, putting more than half of the league in play. And with yesterday's slate also featuring a robust nine games, we have five teams playing today on the second half of a back-to-back: the Boston Celtics, Houston Rockets, Philadelphia 76ers, Phoenix Suns and Washington Wizards.

The Celtics (37-point win over the Mavericks), Rockets (28-point win over the Wizards) and Wizards (28-point loss to the Rockets) all played in blowouts on Sunday so their starters were largely able to play fewer minutes than usual. This could be vital for the possibility of the veterans on these teams such as Paul George, Kevin Durant or Anthony Davis to be available to play both halves of the back-to-back.

The teams won't necessarily announce their full injury report for tonight's games until later today, but each of those vets has played in at least some back-to-backs this season.

George may be the one to watch the most, as he has missed the second-half of both of the Celtics' last two back-to-back sets. Of the other two teams finishing a back-to-back, the Suns don't have any rotation players that tend to sit one-half of consecutive sets ... but the 76ers do. Joel Embiid and LeBron James have each sat in one half of every back-to-back the 76ers have played this season.

Embiid sat out yesterday, while LeBron played and notched a near triple-double with 15 points, 11 assists and 7 rebounds in 33 minutes. Though he is not currently listed on any injury report for tonight I'd expect that LeBron will sit tonight with Embiid likely returning, though of course you should confirm this and all availability questions once the official reports come out.

stories.headline: Crystal Palace appoint Thomas Frank as new head coach
stories.summary: Crystal Palace have appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager after sacking Pierre Sage.
stories.body:
Crystal Palace have appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager after sacking Pierre Sage.

Sage joined in the summer but was sacked after just four months in charge with the club bottom of the Premier League after 10 matches.

Former Brentford and Tottenham manager Frank has signed a three-year contract with Palace.

In a statement on the Palace website, chairman Steve Parish said: "I'm delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace. He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

"I'm confident Thomas' extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season."

Thomas Frank said: "It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
There is just a pair of NHL games Monday, with many teams resting up for the requisite packed schedule Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday (the latter of which again will include 28 teams in action).

Two Eastern teams that appear playoff-bound will square off first, before a rising Western team looks to rebound after a five-game winless streak.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Montreal Canadiens at New York Rangers

7:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | MTL -115, O/U: 6.5

If the season ended after Sunday's games, the Canadiens would be the No. 2 seed in the Atlantic Division, and the Rangers would have a first-round playoff matchup against the rival New Jersey Devils as the Metro's No. 3 seed.

But there are many more games this season, including this one at Madison Square Garden that pits two of the NHL's Original Six franchises.

The Canadiens enter with a handful of key players injured, including Mike Matheson, Josh Anderson, Ivan Demidov and Chris Kreider. Kreider made his mark as a Ranger -- particularly in the playoffs -- but fans will have to hope these teams meet in the postseason to greet him, as he's out for six to eight weeks after suffering an injury Thursday against the Bruins.

Rangers fans might not have much sympathy on the medical front, considering that franchise goalie Igor Shesterkin remains out for the season. The team likely won't have defensemen Alberts Smits and Sean Durzi as well on Monday.

So how will the first game between these teams go? The Canadiens have gone 4-1-0 against the two teams' common opponents thus far (the Bruins, Red Wings, Mammoth, Capitals and Maple Leafs), and the Rangers have gone 2-3-0.

Vancouver Canucks at Utah Mammoth

9:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -360, O/U: 6.5

The Mammoth made their statement in 2025-26, earning a playoff spot and giving the eventual Western Conference champion Vegas Golden Knights a tough series before bowing out in Round 1.

Expectations were high for 2026-27 -- and things started well: The Mammoth charged out to a 6-2-0 record in their first eight games.

The next eight games alternated between wins and losses (not a great sign), before their current five-game winless streak (an even worse sign). The good news? They face the Canucks on Monday.

Vancouver last won Oct. 27; that's four days before Halloween and three days before Nikita Kucherov requested a trade. In the interim, the Canucks have offered teams a chance to "get right" following losing streaks. How nice.

Will the Mammoth get themselves back on track -- and extend the Canucks' losing streak to eight? Or is it time for some real self-reflection in Salt Lake City?

stories.headline: Every MLB team's chance of signing Skubal -- and their backup plans
stories.summary: Dodger or Met blue? We break down all 30 clubs' chances of landing the offseason's biggest free agent -- and who their Plan B should be.
stories.body:
Tarik Skubal is the golden ticket in the 2026-27 MLB free agent class. In what is viewed as a weak group of free agents, the two-time Cy Young Award winner is the clear difference-maker, a pitcher with a 2.42 ERA over the past three seasons.

The state of modern pitching is at an interesting inflection. While starters are throwing harder than ever -- with even more unhittable breaking balls and a wider variety of pitches -- it is also arguably harder than ever to fill 162 starts in a season, let alone fill enough quality innings. In 2026, 377 different pitchers started a game -- an average of 12.6 per team -- and Michael Wacha was the only pitcher to throw 200 innings.

Ten years ago, there were 310 different pitchers who started a game and 15 pitchers who reached 200 innings. Twenty years ago, those figures were 303 starters and 45 who reached 200 innings. Forty years ago, it was 9.6 starters per team and 52 who pitched 200 innings -- and a total of 82 who pitched 162 innings compared to just 46 in 2026.

You get the idea: An ace starter on Skubal's level is a special addition to any roster. Of course, with Skubal perhaps in line for a $300 million contract, not every team has the same odds of signing him -- although, who knows, a new labor deal could drastically change how these deals unfold.

With that, let's introduce the Skubal Tiers -- breaking all 30 teams into tiers on their likelihood of landing Skubal. And since every team needs pitching help of some sort, we'll include a reasonable backup pitching plan for each team.

Note: References to projected contracts are from Kiley McDaniel's ranking of the top 50 free agents, while references to a team's payroll are drawn from the roster resource section at FanGraphs.

Tier 5: There is absolutely no shot

The teams in this tier are mostly the ones you would expect: the so-called small-market teams with owners unwilling to spend big in free agency (despite San Diego having proved a higher-spending approach is possible). Even a new system with a salary floor is unlikely to change habits overnight, so we'll go straight to the backup pitching plans for these teams.

30. Colorado Rockies

Backup plan: Zac Gallen. It's not that the Rockies never sign free agent starters -- heck, just last year they signed Jose Quintana, Tomoyuki Sugano and Michael Lorenzen -- it's just that they haven't signed a premium free agent starter since Mike Hampton in 2001 (at $121 million, that remains the second-biggest free agent contract in Rockies history). Those veterans last offseason were all signed to one-year deals, so the Rockies are basically in the same situation, looking to fill out a rotation with pitchers that no other team really wants.

29. Athletics

Backup plan: Shota Imanaga. Back in 1993 -- let's see, that was 33 years ago -- the A's re-signed free agents Mark McGwire and Ruben Sierra to identical five-year, $28 million contracts. The 1993 A's proceeded to go 68-94, and maybe that scared them off forever from signing top-tier free agents. Believe it or not, the A's have since signed only two free agents to bigger contracts: Billy Butler for $30 million in 2015 and Luis Severino for $67 million in 2025. That's the long way of saying Skubal is not going to West Sacramento. But Imanaga fits the Severino mold of overpaying for a mid-rotation starter.

28. Cincinnati Reds

Backup plan: Kris Bubic/Dustin May. The Reds need a starter to replace Hunter Greene, who will miss the entire season after Tommy John surgery, but the top 10 highest free agent contracts in franchise history don't even add up to Skubal's projected $352 million contract. To the Reds' credit, they did at least sign Chase Burns to a $105 million extension. They can dip into the less expensive tier of starters like Bubic (projected deal of two years, $18 million) or May (one year, $14 million).

27. Miami Marlins
Backup plan: Raisel Iglesias. Since Bruce Sherman bought the team in 2017, the most the Marlins have paid for a free agent is Jorge Soler's $36 million deal -- so, no, Skubal isn't taking his talents to Little Havana, South Beach, Coral Gables, Key Biscayne, Fort Lauderdale or anywhere else in South Florida. The Marlins were middle of the pack in both rotation ERA and bullpen ERA, but will need a closer to replace Pete Fairbanks, so that's probably a priority over a starter (assuming they don't trade Sandy Alcantara and open up a hole). Iglesias is doable on a one-year, $14 million deal.

26. Kansas City Royals

Backup plan: Chris Bassitt/Kevin Gausman. The Royals dug into the pitching market back in 2024, signing Michael Wacha and Seth Lugo -- and the pair helped them win a wild card that season. Both even later signed extensions, and Wacha was the only pitcher in the majors to reach 200 innings in 2026. The Royals do need rotation help after ranking 25th in ERA, and Bassitt is the kind of low-cost vet they can get on a one-year deal. If they want to get more aggressive, Gausman has better strikeout stuff than Bassitt, and his projected three-year, $51 million deal won't break the payroll.

25. Minnesota Twins

Backup plan: Steven Okert/Jason Adam. To improve on a rotation that ranked 22nd in ERA, the Twins will hope Pablo Lopez is ready after missing all of 2026 due to Tommy John surgery. A rotation with Lopez, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley, Dean Kremer and the Bailey Ober/Zebby Matthews/Connor Prielipp group has promise and depth. If anything, the Twins might trade one of Ryan, Kremer or Ober, who are all in their final season before free agency. In the meantime, Minnesota's offseason pitching focus will be the bullpen, which it avoided addressing last offseason.

24. Cleveland Guardians

Backup plan: Casey Mize. The Guardians return their five regular starters from 2026, but might still look to upgrade the back of the rotation -- and perhaps look to trade Tanner Bibee. The five-year, $48 million contract Bibee signed a few years ago starts ramping up in cost, as he's due $7.4 million in 2027, $10.4 million in 2028 and $21.4 million in 2029. The Guardians traded infielder Andres Gimenez when his deal reached this point, so a similar decision could be made with Bibee. Mize could be a great add-low move after he struggled the final two months with the Padres.

23. Houston Astros

Backup plan: Nick Martinez/Nick Pivetta. Skubal to the Astros? That would be like signing up for Napoleon's army right before the Battle of Waterloo. If the Astros are going to give $300 million to anyone, it will be with an extension for 2026 AL MVP Yordan Alvarez, not a free agent from another team (the biggest free agent contract since Jim Crane bought the team has been Josh Hader's $95 million deal). That said, the rotation was a mess, finishing 27th in ERA and last in walk rate. New general manager Randy Flores has a tough task to improve this pitching staff, but given the walk problems, adding a strike-thrower like Martinez or Pivetta is the way to go.

Tier 4: It's not likely ... but it sure would be fun

22. Pittsburgh Pirates

The owners' latest salary cap proposal included a salary floor of $180.2 million. The Pirates' payroll currently sits at an estimated $129 million after finishing 2026 at $109 million. So, umm, the Pirates could maybe afford Skubal in a different world than currently exists and can dream of a 1-2 duo of Skubal and Paul Skenes.

Backup plan: David Peterson/Erick Fedde. The rotation has the potential to improve significantly from last year's No. 14 ranking in ERA -- especially Skenes and Bubba Chandler, who had a promising if erratic rookie season. Mitch Keller is coming off a shoulder injury and a 5.29 ERA, but he's signed for two more years, so Pittsburgh isn't going to be eager to push him out. Still, adding a veteran swingman/sixth starter seems prudent.

21. Los Angeles Angels

With Stan Kroenke coming on as the new owner -- the sale won't be officially approved until January -- maybe there will be a new era of Angels baseball where, if Skubal remains unsigned before the lockout, Kroenke comes out and makes an offer Skubal can't refuse. More realistic: Good luck convincing Skubal to sign with a team that hasn't had a winning record since 2015.

Backup plan: High-leverage relievers. The Angels don't have a head of baseball operations yet, with former Cardinals exec John Mozeliak currently in an interim role, so it might be a slow offseason in Anaheim. If they do make any significant pitching moves, it's more likely to be to upgrade a bullpen that ranked 22nd in ERA and 30th in win probability added.

20. Washington Nationals

The Nationals do have plenty of payroll space for a franchise-altering signing, sitting on an estimated $84 million payroll. Maybe Skubal believes they're heading in the right direction. Maybe they are!

Backup plan: Freddy Peralta/Kaima Taira/Trevor Rogers. With so much payroll flexibility and a bad rotation, the Nationals are likely to do something significant and should go after the best of the non-Skubal starters. Peralta (No. 3), Taira (No. 7) and Rogers (No. 10) rank in the top 10 of available free agents and, importantly for the still-building Nationals, will each be 30 or younger on Opening Day.

19. Baltimore Orioles

Maybe Skubal is a big fan of crab cakes and Edgar Allan Poe.

Backup plan: Kevin Gausman/Tyler Mahle/Nick Pivetta. Baltimore's rotation wasn't as bad as perceived -- 17th in ERA, sixth in innings -- but Trevor Rogers and Chris Bassitt are free agents, so the Orioles need at least one replacement (they do have a bunch of prospects in the high minors ready to compete for rotation spots). These three vets fit into a similar projected salary range of three years, $50 million.

18. Atlanta Braves

Skubal plus Chris Sale plus a healthy Spencer Strider would rekindle memories of Greg Maddux, John Smoltz and Tom Glavine.

Backup plan: Sonny Gray. Alas, the Braves just don't do these monster deals in free agency. They've extended several of their own players to nine-figure contracts, but B.J. Upton's $75 million contract in 2013 remains the biggest free agent signing in franchise history. Gray, a Tennessee native, would love to pitch closer to home, and a projected two-year, $42 million deal fits the Braves.

17. San Francisco Giants

The Giants have obviously had trouble luring marquee free agents in recent years, making aggressive pursuits of Bryce Harper, Aaron Judge and Shohei Ohtani since 2019. Coming off a 65-97 season, it won't be easy to lure Skubal to the Bay Area -- and the rotation's problems suggest they may need to spread money around anyway.

Backup plan: Freddy Peralta/Clay Holmes/Michael King/Shota Imanaga. With Logan Webb missing time, not a single Giants starter pitched 162 innings to qualify for the ERA list. The rotation finished 24th in ERA, 25th in strikeout rate and 23rd in walk rate -- and those numbers look even worse after factoring in their home park. Trevor McDonald, Carson Whisenhunt and Blade Tidwell are already out for 2027. With holes to fill, look for the Giants to make a run at those top non-Skubal starters.

16. Texas Rangers

Before the last lockout in 2021-2022, the Rangers made two huge signings right before it began, locking up Corey Seager for $325 million and Marcus Semien for $175 million. Could they make a shocking splash like that again?

Backup plan: Tyler Mahle. President of baseball operations Chris Young recently told local media that the Rangers plan a payroll "very similar" to 2026, which leaves about $20 million to maneuver -- and they need to address the lineup. They could look to flip Seager (which won't be easy, with five years left on his deal at $31.5 million per season), Jacob deGrom (he's making $37 million) or Nathan Eovaldi (making $24 million) to clear some payroll space. Young hinted he's open to some trades -- "there will be changes," he said -- although all three of those players have no-trade protection. The Rangers were 16th in rotation ERA, but just 24th in road ERA. Bringing back Mahle would be an upgrade over Jack Leiter or Kumar Rocker.

Tier 3: Maybe, but they don't really need a starter

15. Milwaukee Brewers

The Brewers' projected payroll sits right about where it was in 2026. Even if there is room to go a little higher following their title, that might go into locking up World Series MVP William Contreras on a long-term deal before he heads to free agency following the 2027 season. In the meantime, while they did make a deal for Dustin May for temporary rotation help down the stretch in 2026, they have depth here with Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson, Robert Gasser, Kyle Harrison, Shane Drohan, Brandon Sproat and the hopeful return of Quinn Priester. Heck, they could even try Aaron Ashby again as a starter, plus Chad Patrick is around as a reliable swingman.

Backup plan: Trade Trevor Megill? Knowing the way the Brewers operate, Megill is a trade possibility as he enters his final season before free agency. With Abner Uribe or Ashby more than capable of stepping in as closer, Megill could be flipped for ... the next Trevor Megill.

14. Seattle Mariners

The rotation has declined from its 2024 performance (3.38 ERA up to 4.05 in 2026), but this was still a group that at least led the majors in innings pitched. Luis Castillo got traded at the deadline with rookie Kade Anderson ready to step in after his late-season audition. Ryan Sloan is another top prospect who could make an impact in the second half. Indeed, the Mariners might look to make a trade here -- Logan Gilbert, with one more year of team control, would be the big ask, with George Kirby and Bryce Miller lesser options.

Backup plan: Bryan Abreu/Pete Fairbanks. The Mariners do need to revamp their bullpen. They're certainly familiar with Abreu, who would give them a power arm from the right side to set up Andres Munoz. Abreu had a terrible first half for the Astros but was back on track in the second half with a 1.71 ERA.

13. Philadelphia Phillies

The Phillies will once again rely on the big three of Cristopher Sanchez, Zack Wheeler and Jesus Luzardo for their playoff hopes, plus Aaron Nola and Andrew Painter. There isn't much depth past those five starters, but president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski must address the lineup (and hopefully improve the defense as well). A right-handed-hitting outfielder tops that list, and there is a hole in the infield with Luis Arraez and Alec Bohm free agents.

Backup plan: Adrian Morejon/Alex Vesia. Alas, the bullpen -- Phillies fans have heard this before -- still needs help behind closer Jhoan Duran. Jose Alvarado's struggles left the Phillies without a reliable lefty in the bullpen, a void Morejon (second in strikeouts among left-handed relievers the past two seasons) or Vesia (fifth) can fill.

12. New York Yankees

With everyone back from a rotation that led the majors in ERA this past season and ranked third in strikeout rate -- Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodon, Will Warren and Ryan Weathers, plus Clarke Schmidt, Luis Gil and Elmer Rodriguez as depth -- the Yankees have the top projected rotation for 2027 and have other needs to fill.

Backup plan: Adrian Morejon/re-signing David Bednar and Paul Blackburn. Bringing back Bednar as the closer is a top priority (the Yankees gave him a qualifying offer), with re-signing Blackburn right up there, too, following his big season as Bednar's top setup guy. Finally, adding the power-armed Morejon would be the cherry on top.

11. Boston Red Sox

Even after Sonny Gray opted out of his player option, the Red Sox have a rotation with Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle, Brayan Bello and Jake Bennett, with Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo ready to go coming off injuries. Deadline trades depleted more depth -- Connelly Early to the Nationals for Curtis Mead, as well as prospects Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon to the Orioles for Adley Rutschman -- but Boston's top offseason priority will focus on the lineup.

Backup plan: Maybe a reliever? Boston's bullpen was actually very good, ranking second in ERA behind the Yankees, and all the key guys will return. But you can never have too many relievers, and the Red Sox had some surprising performers who might not be able to repeat their 2026 numbers.

Tier 2: The long shots

10. Tampa Bay Rays

OK, this is certainly a long shot -- the highest free agent contract the Rays have given was a $40 million deal for Zach Eflin, but imagine a new world with a salary floor. Maybe the Rays operate like they always have, except now they can add one big superstar to the payroll.

Alternatively, they could also trade Drew Rasmussen -- making $20 million in the final year of his contract -- to acquire prospects or younger starters, and then use some of that money to go after Skubal. By the way, Rasmussen's $20 million salary would be the highest single-season salary in franchise history.

Backup plan: Re-sign Nick Martinez. The veteran right-hander needs a good defense behind him given his low strikeout rate, which is why he's a better fit for Tampa Bay than other teams (he went 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA for the Rays in 2026). He turned down his $20 million player option, looking for a multiyear deal, which the Rays should consider giving him.

9. St. Louis Cardinals

The Cardinals never play in this end of the pool -- Matt Holliday is the only $100 million free agent they've signed, and that was a re-signing situation -- but they do have enormous payroll flexibility and a young, up-and-coming roster to sell Skubal on. St. Louis' rotation was 24th in strikeout rate and 26th in batting average allowed, lacking starters with swing-and-miss stuff.

Backup plan: Freddy Peralta/Kaima Taira/Trevor Rogers/Tyler Mahle. In lieu of Skubal, the Cardinals should at least be in on the next group of starters. Taira is a fascinating option coming over from Japan, a 5-foot-8 right-hander who gets ridiculous extension despite his short stature and has a four-seam fastball that sits 94-97 mph with good shape.

8. Arizona Diamondbacks

The Diamondbacks have gone down this road before, making Zack Greinke the highest-paid pitcher with a $206 million deal in 2016 and then signing Corbin Burnes to a $210 million deal two offseasons ago. That deal quickly backfired when Burnes blew out his elbow 11 starts into his Arizona tenure, returning to make just three starts in 2026. With four years still left on Burnes' contract, it seems unlikely the Diamondbacks would give another risky megadeal to a starting pitcher -- but maybe owner Ken Kendrick will sell off his baseball card collection to do it. (Hey, don't scoff: It's valued at $130 million-plus.)

Backup plan: Foster Griffin/re-signing Michael Soroka. This level of starter is more likely what the Diamondbacks will look for to fill the rotation, with Griffin (two years, $30 million) and Soroka (two years, $24 million) offering similar contract projections.

7. Chicago Cubs

Reports surfaced that the Cubs won't be pursuing Skubal. If so, that's somewhat understandable, since they have an entire rotation to fill given all their free agents (Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Kevin Gausman, Shota Imanaga, David Peterson) as well as Cade Horton likely to miss much of 2027 and Ben Brown's return uncertain following neck surgery.

It's worth noting that while the Cubs gave nine-figure deals to Alex Bregman and Dansby Swanson this decade, their biggest free agent deal in team history remains Jason Heyward's $184 million contract from the 2015-16 offseason. Outfielders Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ are also free agents, complicating the decision-making even if Chicago's payroll currently sits about $115 million below last season.

Backup plan: Freddy Peralta/Trevor Rogers/re-sign Holmes. Of the departing free agents, bringing back Holmes makes the most sense. His ground ball style is a good fit with Nico Hoerner, Bregman and Swanson in the infield. Boyd could be a cheaper alternative, while it might be time to move on from the homer-prone Imanaga. What the Cubs have lacked is a power pitcher to headline a rotation. Hmm, maybe there is room for Skubal and another starter.

6. Detroit Tigers

Why not? The Tigers' luxury tax payroll sits at $192 million compared to 2026's total of $230 million. Sure, Skubal would push the total past that, but not over any potential salary cap, and the roster is otherwise pretty set. Factor in that the two highest-paid players on the roster are Framber Valdez, who is signed for just two more seasons, and Javier Baez, whose deal finally runs out after 2027. That gives the Tigers payroll flexibility into the future -- and can entice Skubal to return to Detroit with a roster that already has a young foundation with Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark, plus other top-100 prospects on the way.

Backup plan: Emilio Pagan? Detroit's bullpen had problems, ranking 12th in ERA but 26th in win probability added -- so, that could be the entire focus with the front office comfortable enough with a rotation featuring Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan. Pagan, the Reds' closer the past two seasons, has agreed to a one-year, $11 million deal with the Tigers, but he's hardly a sure bet to be a step up from Kenley Jansen, so another move or two here makes sense.

5. Chicago White Sox

Why not? Chicago is young, fun, exciting and needs an ace. Like the Cardinals, the White Sox have plenty of payroll space and no guaranteed money on the docket beyond 2027. They'd have to convince Skubal that the club's 2026 success was just the first step to a brighter future -- and convince owner Jerry Reinsdorf to offer Skubal a deal he can't refuse. That might be the hard part: Andrew Benintendi's ill-advised $75 million deal a few years ago is the largest free agent contract in White Sox history.

Backup plan: Freddy Peralta/Trevor Rogers/Clay Holmes/Nick Pivetta. OK, Jeff Passan says the White Sox won't be in on Skubal, even though "they absolutely should be." Agreed. Anyway, even though they announced Grant Taylor will be moving to the rotation, they should still be in on the other top starters. Then, the White Sox will need to replace Taylor's valuable innings in the bullpen, so they should be in on all the top relievers as well.

Tier 1: The favorites

4. Toronto Blue Jays

The Blue Jays went big after Shohei Ohtani. They went after Juan Soto. It wouldn't be shocking then, even though they finished last in the majors in runs scored, to see them go after Skubal. The Jays were middle of the pack (15th) in rotation ERA but just 28th in innings pitched, and while they added Jose Soriano at the trade deadline and will be counting on Cody Ponce returning from his ACL injury, Skubal and Dylan Cease would make for a dynamic duo.

Plus, this isn't the best offseason to be adding offense anyway, so maybe the Jays go all-in on a dominant pitching staff.

Backup plan: Kevin Gausman. On the other hand, with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. entering the second year of his $500 million contract and coming off a nine-homer, 57-RBI season, the Jays might find it too risky to have both Guerrero and a $300 million-plus pitcher on the roster. Gausman enjoyed his time in Toronto and could return on a projected three-year, $51 million deal.

3. San Diego Padres

The Padres are viewed as the big wild card in the Skubal sweepstakes. They have an entire rotation in free agency -- Michael King, Walker Buehler, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray, Casey Mize, Lucas Giolito -- so will have to do some heavy lifting to plug all the gaps. "We're all-in," new owners Kwanza Jones and Jose E. Feliciano said at their introductory news conference in August.

Will that translate into a megadeal for Skubal? Given the complications of the Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts contracts, which run through 2033 for two players on the downturn of their careers, the need to win now is glaringly acute. The potential decline of the team in a couple of years, however, could make Skubal wary about signing here.

Backup plan: Re-signing King. It's been a good match the past three seasons and King's projected deal -- three years, $79.5 million -- is a quarter of Skubal's projection for a pitcher who nearly matched Skubal in WAR in 2026. Indeed, the holes in the rotation will require multiple signings, so maybe the rational move is spreading the Skubal money to two or three pitchers.

2. New York Mets

As with Soto a couple of years ago, if owner Steve Cohen wants someone, money won't be the issue. The Mets were 23rd in rotation ERA in 2026, with little certainty for 2027 beyond Nolan McLean and Christian Scott. President of baseball operations David Stearns isn't a fan of long-term pitching contracts, but the Mets will throw all logic aside in trying to turn things around after a losing season. The payroll will take a big drop after 2027, when Sean Manaea ($25 million), Jorge Polanco ($23 million) and Kodai Senga ($14 million) come off the books.

As Passan pointed out, "Even if a salary cap is in place after the upcoming collective bargaining negotiations reach their conclusion, the Mets can sign Skubal and remain under the cap. They'd be top-heavy, sure, but with money to offload to teams that would need to reach a floor."

Backup plan: Nick Martinez/Michael King/Trevor Rogers. Martinez is the opposite of Skubal -- a finesse right-hander -- but he's a good clubhouse guy, which the Mets need after some of the issues this past season, and proved he can handle a starter's workload after pitching 180 innings for the Rays in 2026. Martinez can be had on a reasonable two-year deal that wouldn't blow up the payroll, perhaps allowing the Mets to bring in a second free agent starter like King or Rogers.

1. Los Angeles Dodgers

As Alden Gonzalez reported, Skubal loved his time with the Dodgers, becoming best buddies with Blake Snell along the way and appreciating a veteran clubhouse dedicated to trying to win a World Series. "Incredible organization, incredible teammates, incredible fanbase," Skubal said after the Dodgers were eliminated in the NLCS. "Honored to wear the L.A. across your chest and on the hat."

Yes, the Dodgers' estimated luxury tax payroll already sits at $386 million for 2027 and a potential salary cap would require some tricky roster machinations down the road -- depending on how a cap might be rolled out -- but this is the Dodgers. Right now, nothing prevents them from spending as much money as necessary to re-sign Skubal.

In the short term, they would love to trade Teoscar Hernandez (making $22.1 million in 2027), not just to clear payroll space but to open up an outfield spot for Josue De Paula.
